fullText:
Residents of Dalby may soon live beside a $31bn datacentre. The premier sees ‘opportunity’ for the state – but others fear AI’s global creep

From the veranda on his bush block, Denver Kanowski has watched resources companies come and go from rural Queensland for 70 years.

The home cost him $800, and lets him live how he likes, in nature. It’s also in the middle of a gasfield, not far from the Linc Energy contamination site, down the road from a coalmine and three gas power plants.

Last month came the biggest scheme yet, a $31bn datacentre to power Claude, the large language model developed by global AI giant Anthropic. If built, Australia’s largest datacentre would be about 15 minutes’ drive away from Kanowski’s home, outside Kogan, near Dalby, about 180km west of Brisbane.

In a community that has seen the boom and bust of coal seam gas, the response from many has been the same as Kanowski’s: once bitten, twice shy.

“This is the power of money and the power of greed and shortsighted stupidity,” Kanowski says.

Anthropic’s project is to be built on a 725-hectare plot of land now occupied by a 24,000 head feedlot, surrounded by gas wells.

According to Singapore-based developer Zerra DC, its cooling system will be far less water intensive than most existing datacentres’, generating about the same demand as an average shopping centre.

But like all AI, it will require an enormous amount of energy. The Western Downs datacentre will require a peak power capacity equal to about a quarter of total state energy demand, 2.16GW. It would also employ thousands during construction, with about 1,400 long-term jobs, according to the company.

The proposal was made public just last month.

Within days, Dalby travel agent Mordechai Winters had made up his mind: he didn’t want it.

“I was crushed. You know, it’s very disappointing that the council and also the government would consider it,” he says.

Issues like energy demand, noise and poor siting have driven a massive backlash against datacentres in the United States. Three-quarters of Americans now oppose them, and more than 500 counties have imposed a ban.

At least thousands have a similar view in Australia.

A petition that Winters helped to launch has been signed by more than 21,500 people – mostly from the area – in just a few weeks, he says.

He believes the project’s benefits are exaggerated and will trigger the same boom-bust cycle as gas.

Cecil Plains farmer Liza Balmain remembers the big – and eventually unrealised – promises of the gas industry when it arrived.

The industry brought massive change; academics later concluded that its scale and pace in a small agricultural community “was likely unprecedented anywhere in the world”. There was a huge influx of workers, with the high wages of gas attracting labour away from farms and local business.

Then – because setting up a gas well requires a lot more labour than operating it – the industry left, just as quickly as it had arrived, leaving business owners with debts they couldn’t pay on investments they no longer needed. Some academics believe the industry left the region worse off. Others think it was a slim net positive.

Balmain, who led a long campaign against the gas industry, says she can see “huge similarities” between the coal seam gas era and the proposed datacentre.

Australians across the country are concerned. Jo Shulman, CEO of the Environmental Defenders Office which has long helped communities fight resources projects such as coal seam gas, says the group had seen a 250% increase in queries about datacentres to the service’s free legal advice line since January.

“I would say the datacentre is the new frontier,” she says.

“Communities are concerned about [their] impacts on the environment and their wellbeing”.

Shulman says datacentres will form an essential part of the clean energy transition – but called for a pause to allow national standards to catch up.

“We think that there should be a moratorium on any further datacentres, or they risk repeating the same things that we saw with the coal seam gas boom,” she says.

The Dalby mayor, Andrew Smith, says the ultimate authority over the region’s largest ever project should rest with the Western Downs regional council, population 35,452. Speaking to Guardian Australia last month, he said council did not expect the project to be taken over by the state coordinator general.

“We did ask the question, but our understanding is it will stay with local government,” he says.

But then, on Friday, things changed. The state announced it would take datacentres out of the hands of local councils, under a new planning framework to ensure “a consistent and transparent framework across the state,” similar to the government’s renewables planning policy.

“We will treat these projects no worse and no better than we do mining, renewables or tourism projects. Any deals done must be with the backing of councils and communities,” a spokesperson for planning minister, Jarrod Bleijie, says.

“The state government will become the responsible assessor and coordinator of any data centre applications, instead of local councils”.

If given the green light, the project will be worth more to the local community than coal seam gas, he says.

“In general, the coal seam gas industry has been wonderful for our region. It’s diversified our economy, which we talk about a lot. It’s created jobs,” he says.

“Prior to coal seam gas, we were exporting a lot of our clever kids, because the opportunities weren’t back in the region.”

Anthropic wants to start using the centre as early as next year. But Smith says the planning couldn’t be rushed – and was careful not to endorse or oppose the project.

The Queensland premier, David Crisafulli, lobbied the company to invest in the state during a recent trade mission, he told parliament last week.

Crisafulli said the state would help the council assess the project, but said it had done an excellent job with the gas industry and could do so again.

“They see the same opportunity I do, and that opportunity is to make sure that there are jobs, very good jobs in regional areas, and if we get it right, lower power bills for every other Queenslander as well. I see a really good play with that,” the premier said.

Toowoomba and Surat Basin Enterprise chief executive officer Jo Sheppard says most residents of the area had not yet made up their minds about the project, but that it was important for the developer to maintain their social license.

She added it was a “a once in a generation opportunity for Western Downs region and our broader region”, with the power to transform the town from a “ “fairly quiet” farming community to something more, adding to booms triggered by gas, and then renewables.

“Someone actually did say to me the other day: ‘Gosh, should we all be buying a house in Dalby?’”

Kanowski says there was something different about the datacentre compared with coal and coal seam gas schemes. He believes it will go beyond harming the environment by contributing to an online “fantasy” world, disconnecting people from the things that genuinely matter.

“[The datacentre developers] don’t even see the trees. They don’t understand the relationship between all the things. This is my world, I love it,” he says.

“This is not a datacentre … This is part of a network that these money-crazed idiots are planning to put all over the planet.”

title: Wu wins first title since Crucible as Chinese snooker hits new high
description: Wu Yize claims his first ranking title since he became world champion - a result that means China will have the top two players in the rankings for the first time.
fullText:
Wu Yize secured his first ranking title since becoming world champion with a 10-5 win over Yuan Sijun in an all-Chinese final at the Shenzhen Open.

A profitable week for 22-year-old Wu pushes him to a career high of second place in the world rankings, behind Zhao Xintong.

It means that China has the leading two players in the rankings for the first time, further illustrating the country's position as a snooker superpower.

Wu became the second-youngest player to lift snooker's most coveted title at the Crucible when he beat Shaun Murphy in May, and he followed that up with a composed performance to see off surprise finalist Yuan at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.

Having demolished Judd Trump 6-1 in the semi-finals, Wu had early breaks of 117 and 80 to move 3-1 ahead against Yuan.

But, playing in his first ranking final, Yuan then reeled off three frames in a row.

Wu responded with two more half-centuries in the final frames of the opening session to take a 5-4 lead in the best-of-19 match.

Prospects of a tight final all the way to the finish line soon evaporated.

World champion Wu returned with breaks of 74 and 62 to take control at 8-5 in the evening session as Yuan struggled with his safety play.

And there was no way back for Yuan, 26, as Wu made sure of the trophy and the £177,000 top prize.

title: Evans claims dramatic WRC title after Solberg crash
description: Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashes in the final moments of Rally Italia Sardegna.
fullText:
Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashed in a dramatic finish to the Rally Italia Sardegna.

Sweden's Solberg was on course to snatch the lead on the final stage of the last round of the World Rally Championship (WRC) when he crashed with less than 100 metres to go.

"It hasn't sunk in," said a shocked Evans, who became the first British world champion in 25 years.

"I was sure it was over. I feel for Oliver, he had an incredible weekend. I don't know what to say."

The 37-year-old and co-driver Scott Martin had led for much of the 2026 season and took a 21-point advantage into the final round in Sardinia.

But that gap had shrunk to a solitary point by the time the drivers lined up for the last of 17 stages, bringing back painful memories of previous narrow misses for Evans.

Solberg, 25, needed only to beat his Toyota team-mate in the final stage to claim enough bonuses to be champion, but crashed two corners from the finish.

Evans becomes only the third British man to win the WRC title after Colin McRae in 1995 and Richard Burns in 2001.

Relive dramatic final stage shootout for title as it happened

The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory

Solberg, whose father Petter won the WRC title in 2003, won the rally by almost a minute ahead of nine-time world champion Sebastien Ogier.

He and English co-driver Elliott Edmondson were also on course to win the final stage and collect a maximum 35 points for the weekend to take the title by two points.

However, his crash meant he finished five points behind Evans in the overall standings.

A third Toyota driver, Sami Pajari, finished a further one point behind in third - having seen his own title challenge evaporate on the final weekend.

An inconsolable Solberg remained in his car for some time at the end of the stage before being encouraged to take to the podium by Gazoo Racing team principal Jari-Matti Latvala and team-mate Ogier.

"Two corners, two corners," said an emotional Solberg.

"First congratulations to Elfyn, he has been very consistent all season. That I even had a shot after my rollercoaster of a season is incredible.

"I tried everything. I knew I was pushing but didn't know if it was enough. I pushed even more and I couldn't save the car. I tried my very best."

Evans, from Dolgellau in north Wales, had previously missed out on the title on the final day three times and in two of those seasons he had taken a lead into the concluding rally before losing out to Ogier in 2020 and 2025.

"I don't really know what my reaction is. It's surreal with how it happened. It's a relief," he said.

"It wouldn't by my proudest way of winning it, but it's job done."

For Toyota sporting director Kaj Lindstrom there were mixed feelings.

"That was the hardest thing. The ending was quite something, I didn't expect it," said the Finn.

"It was a good fight and we all saw that Oliver was all or nothing. It held all the way to the end.

"Oliver still has time but Elfyn finally got his title so we're really happy for him."

The WRC season was reduced to 13 rounds when the Saudi Arabia event, originally planned for next month, was cancelled because of the ongoing unrest in the Middle East.

Rally Italia Sardegna marked the end of Jon Armstrong's rookie season at the top level of WRC, and he produced his best result when finishing seventh.

"It's been good to have a clean weekend with a strong result," said the M-Sport Ford driver.

"It's not been an easy year and this was a rally to show we can put it together. A big thanks to everyone who has been supporting us, it's been a great year and it's been a privilege to drive this car."

Armstrong's team-mate and fellow Irishman Josh McErlean did not fare as well despite running as high as sixth on Saturday before retiring after a collision with a tree.

He also had to stop twice on Sunday before finishing well off the pace but claimed ninth spot in the championship.

title: Liverpool will offload struggling forward: Three clubs want January deal
description: Liverpool strengthened their attack with a couple of new forwards in the summer transfer window. Victor Munoz was onboarded after the Reds triggered the FIFA World Cup winner’s £34m Osasuna release...
fullText:
Liverpool strengthened their attack with a couple of new forwards in the summer transfer window.

Victor Munoz was onboarded after the Reds triggered the FIFA World Cup winner's £34m Osasuna release clause.

And Andoni Iraola also reeled in Bradley Barcola in the closing stages of the window - with the France international arriving for a fee that could reach £123m.

Those signings will no doubt have an impact on forwards already on the books.

One such performer would be Federico Chiesa. The Italian, who turns 29 this month, finds himself well down the pecking order under Iraola this term.

Chiesa hasn't yet managed to make it into a single matchday squad under the Basque tactico having suffered an injury in a preseason friendly against Como.

Under contract until 2028 it has been speculated for a long time that the Euro 2020 winner would be heading back to Serie A. His wages - thought to be around £150k per week - are prohibitive for Italian sides while Liverpool are also insisting on a fee.

That has not stopped speculation ahead of the January transfer window however with three Italian top-flight sides now tracking Chiesa.

According to a report in Calciomercato Chiesa is wanted by champions Inter Milan as well as Lazio and Atalanta.

Describing Chiesa as a "struggling" Liverpool forward the report suggests that the versatile forward views a move back to Serie A as crucial to regaining his place in the national team.

"Federico Chiesa could return to Serie A during the winter transfer window, as the attacking winger continues to struggle to find a place at Liverpool," the report reads.

"Now in his third season in England, Federico Chiesa is ready to return to Serie A to try to find the consistency that could earn him a return to the national team in 2027.

"There are currently no concrete negotiations for the player, but Inter, Atalanta, and Lazio are closely monitoring the situation and could make an attempt for the former Juventus player during the winter transfer window."

Inter came close to landing Chiesa as an alternative to Luis Henrique during the summer window but ultimately the deal fell down.

Chiesa is currently miles off making it under Iraola - with younger players such as Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas now staking a claim for minutes on a more regular basis than the man signed in 2024 for £12.5m from Juventus.

title: Sabalenka stunned by Bartunkova at China Open
description: World number two Aryna Sabalenka follows Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she falls to a surprise defeat by Nikola Bartunkova.
fullText:
World number two Aryna Sabalenka followed Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she fell to a surprise defeat by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova.

It comes a day after top seed Rybakina, who defeated Sabalenka in last month's US Open final and replaced the Belarusian at the top of the rankings, was knocked out by Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva.

Czech Bartunkova sprung another upset at the WTA 1000 tournament and continued her breakthrough season with a 6-4 6-3 over Sabalenka.

"I focused on myself, to be calm," said Bartunkova, who will face Austria's Sinja Kraus next.

"She's a legend, so I'm really happy that I won the match."

It is the first time since 2015 that the top two seeds have failed to reach the round of 16 at the China Open.

Sabalenka has not won a title since completing the 'Sunshine Double' in March, when she triumped at Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back.

It has been a mixed year for Sabalenka by her high standards. She will finish without a Grand Slam trophy for the first time since 2022 and has often struggled to control her frustrations on court.

Against Bartunkova, she failed to convert any of her five break points and she threw her racquet after falling a break down early in the second set.

Alcaraz, the defending champion in Tokyo, saved a set point in the opening set and was leading 7-6 (7-3) 2-1 when the Canadian was forced to withdraw.

It is just Alcaraz's third event since returning from a wrist injury at last month's US Open, where he fell to Ben Shelton in the quarter-finals.

title: Bowie seizing Scotland shot after World Cup disappointment
description: BBC Scotland speaks to Kieron Bowie after he scores his first goal for his country against North Macedonia.
fullText:
Sometimes, the solution to a problem can be hiding in plain sight.

On 19 May, Steve Clarke assembled his collection of players to embark on a World Cup journey.

Despite featuring and scoring for a Hellas Verona side heading for relegation from Serie A, and with a perennial problem of strikers not firing regularly for Scotland, Kieron Bowie was overlooked.

Given the loyalty Clarke showed to those who had served him so well, it was not a huge surprise. Neither was the impotence of the national team in the USA as they conjured up just one John McGinn goal.

"I received a message from him saying that I'm not in the squad but these things happen and it's just about how you bounce back from it to be honest," said Bowie.

"I scored goals in a struggling Verona team and that was as much as I could do. I was happy with where I was at and I was happy with how I'd played.

"I just spent a lot of time at home with my family and then a little golf holiday to Portugal for a week and that was all I did."

Two going on four, five or six on good night for new Scotland era

Scotland beat North Macedonia in Nations League for Pocognoli's first win

Bowie may have been cursing his luck again on Tuesday when his first international start was reduced to a mere 13 minutes following Jack Hendry's red card in the Hampden loss to Switzerland.

The landscape now looks very different.

The former Raith Rovers and Hibernian forward was one of the main Scotland heroes in Skopje after sending a deliciously whipped finish into the net in the 2-0 win over North Macedonia.

Playing in a new 3-4-1-2, Bowie started the game up top with Oli McBurnie in an ultra-attacking line up set out by Sebastien Pocognoli.

Throughout the game, his stats stacked up. The most shots with seven, the most on target with four, most shots in the box with five and the most touches in the opposition box with 11.

"You play all your life to represent a country and to score a goal is just an unbelievable feeling," said the 24-year-old Fifer.

"This manager's come in and he's put a lot of trust in me.

"I think the style that he wants to play definitely plays into my strengths. I think you've seen today a lot of times running them in behind and just showing strength against occupying defenders is one of the main things.

"It's a process but I think everyone's enjoying that process and it's a bit of a change."

The word "process" has been used so many times by the Scotland head coach and his players in recent days it's probably the new team motto.

Pocognoli is trying to implement a radically different system to his predecessor. Not only that, it's a different mindset. All while trying to embed a clutch of new players.

It's early days for the Belgian, his group, and, of course, Bowie. But the man on loan at Sassuolo believes things are clicking, and it's an opportunity for him to make his mark.

"It's a lot longer international break," he explained. "We spend a lot more time together so it's good for him to get his message across and his ideas. Also, we play more games so we have to train a little bit less of course.

"I think for me it's a fresh start with a new coach and different ideas.

"He said to me 'you don't need to prove yourself, just go and do what I know you can do' and I feel like I'm just doing that."

Bowie, who made his Rovers debut at 16, added: "I think people, obviously Scottish fans, have the same idea of how I was when I was at Hibs and that's all they can remember.

"But I feel like since I moved to Serie A, it's a different challenge against more experienced players and at a higher level.

"So, yeah, I feel like I've definitely kicked into another gear and I feel like I'm showing that."

title: Bellingham unlocks new level and potential to be 'one of the greatest'
description: Jude Bellingham's international future was being called into question a year ago, but now he is regarded as potentially one of England's "greatest of all time".
fullText:
Just a year ago, Jude Bellingham's place in the England squad was up in the air. Now he is being talked about as having the potential to be one of football's "greatest of all time".

The Real Madrid man was left out of Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions squad in October 2025 and his place at the World Cup was called into question, with the German head coach saying Bellingham wouldn't get star treatment.

But Bellingham did of course make the squad for the World Cup and was arguably his team's standout performer, finishing as England's top scorer with seven goals as they reached the semi-finals and finished third.

He has already shown that he is world class with starring performances for club and country, but the way he helped England to dismantle Croatia 7-0 in the Nations League on Saturday looked like someone perhaps reaching a new level.

The 23-year-old was instrumental in Rijeka, scoring as well as registering a hat-trick of assists. He even ended the match wearing the captain's armband as England inflicted the heaviest defeat in Croatia's history.

"Bellingham can go on to be one of the greatest players of all time," former Manchester United and Republic of Ireland midfielder Roy Keane said on ITV after the game.

"At this moment in time, he is an amazing footballer. The package – his running power, his delivery, his goal threat. The way he is progressing as a player, I still think there is a lot more to come from him."

Bellingham, recently voted England's player of the year for the second year in a row, is now "nailed on as the 10" for the future, former England defender Matt Upson told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Keane added: "He has been fantastic in possession, but what he does out of possession lifts all these other players.

"If you have a player that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and he's playing for Real Madrid and doing brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball... that will just inspire other players. He is a huge leader for them."

England's front four will share praise for the way in which they demolished the Croatian backline.

Record goalscorer Harry Kane scored twice, as did Bukayo Saka, with Anthony Gordon scoring and assisting too.

And Kane will be back in the spotlight on Tuesday when he can equal Peter Shilton's all-time England men's appearance record against the Czech Republic at Wembley.

In moving to 89 goals for his country, the 33-year-old again showed how irreplaceable he is for England, but, when he was rested with 20 minutes to go, it was Bellingham who took the captain's armband.

And that highlighted the younger man's importance as a leader within the squad.

Bellingham was also directly involved in more than two goals in an England game for the first time, and he became the first player to record three assists in a game for the Three Lions since Trent Alexander-Arnold against San Marino in November 2021.

It was Bellingham's performance in front of goal that impressed former England striker Ian Wright.

"When Bellingham is on the pitch, he is always driving forward and going again and again," Wright said.

"He was involved in everything. His athleticism, his technical ability, his intensity. He never lets up, the way he gets in the box, he is always in there unmarked. He is always in there."

Bellingham showed every aspect of his game against Croatia and Tuchel was asked by BBC Sport if he had gone to another level.

"Yes, at the moment it seems like it, and you always need to," Tuchel said.

"It's like you can never stand still. You have to develop and you have to push for the next level, otherwise other teams will catch up."

Tuchel, who said the performance was a way to "move on" after the disappointment of England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, said that he "adjusted some things" following the tournament, giving players, including Bellingham, "a lot of responsibility".

Saka was part of the front four and Bellingham assisted his first goal with a high quality cross.

"He was amazing tonight," Saka said of Bellingham.

"He deserved player of the year and he deserved man of the match tonight too. He was special.

"[I'm] happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team."

title: Whittaker survives late scare to hold on for points win
description: British light-heavyweight Ben Whittaker survives a dramatic late onslaught from Conor Wallace to move a step closer to a world-title shot with a points victory in Birmingham.
fullText:
British light-heavyweight Ben Whittaker survived a dramatic late onslaught from Conor Wallace to move a step closer to a world-title shot with a points victory in Birmingham.

The 29-year-old controlled much of the contest with his trademark showboating and superior boxing skill at the Utilita Arena before Wallace came roaring back in the championship rounds.

The Northern Irishman rocked Whittaker in the 10th and came close to a remarkable turnaround in the 12th, with the home fighter forced to hold on until the final bell.

The judges scored it 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113 as Whittaker became mandatory challenger for the IBF world title.

"It was too easy and I took my eye off the ball a little bit. He caught me with a good shot but that's boxing," Whittaker said.

"When it got a bit too easy I was playing too much and doing silly antics."

The Olympic silver medallist extended his unbeaten professional record to 13 wins and one draw and is now mandatory challenger for IBF champion Dmitry Bivol, who also holds the WBA 'super' and WBO belts and is expected to face Liverpool's Callum Smith in December.

Wallace, 30, suffered the second defeat of his 19-fight career and called for an immediate rematch.

"If he wants to run it back and get a beat down again he can. If not, we'll move on," Whittaker responded.

Whittaker made an extravagant entrance, accompanied by a live string ensemble playing WWE star The Undertaker's theme before switching to "Icon" by Karen.

Despite being from nearby West Bromwich, Whittaker was greeted by as many jeers as cheers from the roughly 5,000 fans inside the arena.

The fight came alive in the third when Whittaker briefly staggered Wallace with a shot that skimmed his forehead.

Wallace's travelling support made themselves heard, only to be drowned out by an airhorn smuggled into the arena as Whittaker found his rhythm

Among those in attendance were former UFC champion Leon Edwards and American Cassondra Gainey, who travelled nearly 4,000 miles from North Carolina after Whittaker's social-media videos helped lift her spirits during cancer treatment.

Wallace offered a warning of what was to come when he landed a heavy left in the sixth.

"Stay focused. Just because you're comfortable, don't get lazy," trainer Andy Lee told Whittaker, who regained control before an almost disastrous 10th round.

Wallace hurt him with a thudding southpaw left before Whittaker walked on to a huge shot and looked in serious trouble.

Whittaker briefly got some respite when Wallace was warned for punching on the break, but he continued pushing forward as a major upset suddenly felt possible.

Whittaker hit the canvas three times in the final round, none ruled knockdowns, as Wallace threw everything at a visibly tiring opponent.

"I only have myself to blame," he said. "I feel like I've got the best support in the world. This felt like my home show tonight even though it's in Birmingham."

Promoter Eddie Hearn welcomed the possibility of a rematch: "We know Ben is in the position to fight the winner of Bivol-Smith but it's likely that won't be until next summer, so he needs to fight in the interim."

On a strong undercard showcasing domestic talent, there was British-title success for Walsall's Hamza Uddin and Londoner Bilal Fawaz.

Nigeria-born Fawaz, who is fighting for a British passport, stopped Eithan James in the eighth round to retain his British and Commonwealth light-middleweight titles.

Fawaz – who earned a £5,000 stoppage bonus offered to him by promoter Hearn earlier in the night - called out IBF world champion Josh Kelly and Conor Benn after his win.

"It doesn't matter who is in front of me, with the capacity of what we are trying to achieve, no one can stop us except if they are at world level," Fawaz told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Unbeaten Uddin, 23, dominated Sean Bruce, dropping him twice in the fifth with punishing body and head shots for an eighth straight win.

Uddin closed the show in the eighth with a heavy right. Bruce rose at the count of nine before the referee stepped in.

Given star billing in the chief support on his professional debut, standout amateur Odel Kamara, 22, dominated Thodoris Ritzakis, dropping the Greek in the first before a somewhat premature third-round stoppage.

"Liverpool has a star. Britain has got a star. This kid is going all the way," Hearn said of the debutant.

The Chinese star enjoyed a great 2024 season, winning Olympic gold, reaching the Australian Open final and peaking at world number four. However, an injury-ridden 2025 stunted her progress.

She's bounced back this year, although Zheng still has a long way to go. After her latest win at the China Open, Zheng was asked if she would rather win a Grand Slam title or become world number one.

Never keen to make life easy for herself, Zheng won her first two matches at the China Open in three sets. She defeated Shi Han, 7-6, 4-6, 6-2, and Anna Kalinskaya, 6-7, 6-4, 4-0 (RET).

During her post-match press conference Zheng was asked to update fans on her physical condition, having been seen coughing throughout her second-round win.

"My physical condition starting from the US Open, I've had this cold. I've been coughing, which hasn't recovered yet. I've been using tissues because when the temperature falls, my nose runs, and I need to use tissues. This is something to do with the inflammation of the nose," she said.

Provided she doesn't withdraw from the tournament, Zheng will return to take on Czechia's Marie Bouzkova in round three. Zheng and Bouzkova have never met before, although the Chinese star is 6-10 against Czech opponents on the WTA Tour.

If Zheng can navigate her way past the 18th seed, she will meet Alina Charaeva or Sonay Kartal in the last 16. Zheng would walk on court as a favourite in either match-up.

Looking ahead, she could play Belinda Bencic, Ann Li, Maria Sakkari, or Elina Svitolina in the quarter-finals, then Coco Gauff, Sun Xinran, Jelena Ostapenko, Elise Mertens, Iva Jovic, Kamilla Rakhimova, Donna Vekic, or Iga Swiatek in the semis.

title: Tuchel says rout in Rijeka can help heal England’s World Cup wounds
description: England boss Thomas Tuchel believes the 7-0 hammering of Croatia can help heal the wounds of the World Cup. Tuchel's side dismantled their familiar opponents in the Nations League clash in Rijeka, with a rampant front four of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon making hay.
fullText:
England boss Thomas Tuchel believes the 7-0 hammering of Croatia can help heal the wounds of the World Cup.

Tuchel's side dismantled their familiar opponents in the Nations League clash in Rijeka, with a rampant front four of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Bukayo Saka and Anthony Gordon making hay.

It was the sort of attacking performance that England fans were longing for in the summer, with the pain of the semi-final defeat to Argentina still raw.

But Tuchel said the manner of the display can point towards a brighter future as he said: "This is the only way to move forward, even if you still feel pain.

"You have to play with the pain if you still feel the disappointment, you have to play with it, that is the nature of sport.

"It was not an easy camp in the beginning after this long tournament for multiple reasons.

"But straight away, the first training session on Tuesday, the build-up to the Spain game, we had an excellent performance against Spain but not the result [losing 3-2], the reaction to the result in Czechia [winning 2-0] and now the build-up [here].

"The focus in the meetings, the translation of the meetings onto the pitch and to bring it within these circumstances in Croatia, to win with this dominant performance, that is the way to move on.

"I've said many times, we will always have a scar, we will always feel pain and disappointment. That is the way it is but this is the way to move forward.

"We adjusted some stuff after some things after the World Cup and we played in the same manner in all three matches. We are getting better at it and the team buys into it, this is the most important."

England were irresistible as they inflicted a biggest ever defeat on Croatia, described by Tuchel as a "complete" performance.

Kane and Saka both scored twice and got an assist, Bellingham notched one and made two others, while Gordon scored one and created another. Substitute Morgan Rogers added a late seventh.

Bellingham was the standout player with another virtuoso performance and Tuchel admitted: "At the moment, it seems like [he's gone to another level] and you always need to.

"The level you showed last week is never enough in the next week, that's just the nature of football.

"You can never stand still, If you stand still, it is like (being) on an escalator, If you walk against it, you have to walk to even maintain your level.

"You have to push for the next level, otherwise other teams will catch up. That's why it is always necessary to reach for the next level.

"It was a fantastic victory, the performance was on the highest level from the first to last minute.

"The hunger off the ball was the very highest level. I'm very happy about the attitude. We were never arrogant, always humble. It was a complete 90-minute performance."

Croatia are a far cry from the golden generation which saw them reach the 2018 World Cup final and semi-final four years later.

Slaven Bilic said: "I cannot offer any excuses. England were too good for us. We were not up to the level."

Ireland scored seven tries as they secured a comprehensive 43-19 win over Japan in their Test match at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Saturday.

Scott Bemand's side had defeated the same opponents in a WXV Global Series encounter in Galway the previous weekend.

Ireland recovered from conceding an early try to cross the whitewash four times in the first half to help them to a 22-7 advantage at the break.

Japan rallied but the hosts extended their lead in the second period to ensure they travel to face South Africa for a two-match series in the WXV with confidence high and momentum gathered.

Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett both marked their debuts off the bench with tries.

Ireland had begun their series of autumn matches with a disappointing 40-36 defeat by the USA at Tallaght Stadium but recovered to beat Japan 31-24 in Galway.

The opening minutes of Saturday's contest were marked by a high penalty count on the part of Ireland and Japan took full advantage of their indiscipline as Sakurako Korai barged over from close range after just five minutes.

Emily Lane dotted down soon after but the score was ruled out for an infringement in the build-up.

Prop Eilis Cahill powered over after Ireland worked the ball well through the phases, with Dannah O'Brien's conversion levelling the scores.

Masami Kawamura was sin-binned for cynical play in holding up an attack and Ireland made use of their numerical advantage when Brittany Hogan rumbled over to build on her double try-scoring appearance last week.

Sustained pressure from the home side resulted in two further touchdowns before the interval.

Neve Jones crashed over after some enterprising play and another huge maul effort and then Anna McGann showed strength to stretch and ground the ball after Niamh Gallagher broke through and Erin King provided the pass.

Just two minutes after the resumption, Beibhinn Parsons rode a tackle and went over after a flowing move through the hands as she extended her all-time record of Ireland tries to 25.

Parsons accelerated and dotted down over the try-line, with O'Brien adding the extras.

Teenager Nami Asari led something of a Japan fightback as patient play culminated in her scoring for the second week in a row.

Nijiho Nagata crashed over from another maul to reduce the deficit to 10 but the away side's momentum was halted when Nishi was yellow-carded for head-to-head contact on King.

McInerney shrugged off a couple of attempted tackles and dived over beside the upright after being introduced off the bench.

Then, as the clock ticked into the red, it was the turn of fellow debutant Barrett to pick up and dive across the line for try number seven for her side.

Enya Breen's conversion put 24 points between the teams at the final whistle.

title: Wu thrashes Trump to set up Yuan final in Shenzhen
description: Chinese world champion Wu Yize wins six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 at the Shenzhen Open and set up a final against countryman Yuan Sijun.
fullText:
Reigning world champion Wu Yize won six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 in the Shenzhen Open semi-finals.

Wu, who will leapfrog Trump in the rankings and move second in the world after the final, bounced back in dramatic fashion after losing the opening frame to set up an all-Chinese final against Yuan Sijun at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.

Yuan, 26, endured a much more difficult route to his maiden ranking final, battling through 6-5 against Englishman Jimmy Robertson.

World number two Trump, who won the Shanghai Masters in August, had gone into the Shenzhen semi-final in fine form after beating Mark Selby 5-0 in the last eight.

But after clinching the opening frame with a break of 77, the 2019 world champion handed the initiative to his opponent with a string of errors.

Wu, 22, capitalised to avenge a defeat by Trump at the last-four stage in Shanghai earlier this year, making three breaks of 50 or more in a scrappy encounter before clinching victory with a break of 110.

"When I was preparing for the evening match, I saw that Yuan had shed some tears," Wu told World Snooker Tour.

"I believe it is his first ranking final. Hopefully, we can put on a great match for everyone. Of course, I hope I can take the trophy home, but we will both give it everything we have."

An emotional Yuan found it much more difficult to get over the winning line, with the lead continually changing hands throughout the best-of-11 encounter before his opponent forced a deciding frame that took 50 minutes to complete and saw a total of 177 points scored.

Robertson put Yuan in a difficult snooker on the final red and clawed back 41 penalty points before himself being put in a snooker, with Yuan finally clearing to the pink to earn his place in the final of the inaugural event.

"I feel that my first ranking final has come a little bit late," said Yuan, who started the tournament as the world number 33 but would move to the cusp of the top 16 with victory on Sunday.

"Since the pandemic in 2020, the years in between have been quite difficult, and I feel it hasn't been easy. So after all these years, I just hope I can give myself something to show for it."

title: 'I want to discover Manchester' - Olid hunts recommendations
description: Manchester United manager Eva Olid says she is "asking for recommendations" as she prepares to look around the city for the first time during the international break
fullText:
Manchester United manager Eva Olid says she is "asking for recommendations" as she prepares to look around the city for the first time during the international break.

The Spaniard replaced Marc Skinner two months ago after leaving Hearts but told BBC Sport that she has been so busy working, she has yet to explore her new home.

Having beaten rivals Liverpool on Saturday, United now have a fortnight's break from action while international play-offs for the World Cup take place and Olid is determined to make the most of it.

"I didn't stop from when I arrived!" she said. "Home, work, home, work. My parents are here, my family are here and now I want to discover Manchester."

United's women's team play most of their home matches at Leigh Sports Village, approximately 12 miles west of central Manchester, while they train on the same site as the men at Carrington in Trafford.

Man Utd mark 250th game with narrow win over Liverpool

Despite achieving great success in the Scottish Women's Premier League, Olid arrived at United as an unknown quantity in English football.

She experienced a difficult start too, her team losing to London City Lionesses on the opening night of the Women's Super League season before being thrashed 5-0 at home by Chelsea a week later - managing just two shots on target combined in those games.

However, drawing at Arsenal was promising, and now four straight wins across the WSL and League Cup with 18 goals scored suggests her philosophy is starting to get through.

Not that she is satisfied just yet.

"I am so happy for the players - they deserve it," Olid said. "We have started to click in a lot of things and they fight for each other.

"But there is still a lot to improve. We created chances, but our last pass and our finishing needs to be better. That will come."

Liverpool counterpart Gareth Taylor was less impressed with Olid's tactics, having seen his side's encouraging start to the season stunted by two defeats in their past three.

"They were very direct and we fell into their trap," Taylor said. "Their goalkeeper was literally kicking out of her hands.

"We have got to be braver and there are lessons to learn. This was the first time where we have not been a good reflection of ourselves."

description: At the Formello Training Centre, Lazio played their second friendly of the extended international break, hosting Serie B boys Juve Stabia.Absent Lazio PlayersLazio entered the game without the eight p...
fullText:
At the Formello Training Centre, Lazio played their second friendly of the extended international break, hosting Serie B boys Juve Stabia.

Lazio entered the game without the eight players who were called up for international duty: Christos Mandas, Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen, Josip Sutalo, Kenneth Taylor, Davide Frattesi, Nuno Tavares, and Albert Gudmundsson, who returned early after dislocating his shoulder.

The Iceland star joined Nicolo Rovella, Adam Marusic, Danilo Cataldi, Adrian Przyborek, and Bruno Galassi on the sidelines, while Fisayo Dele-Bashiru made his return to the squad.

Gennaro Gattuso once again tested a 4-2-3-1 formation while keeping the same lineup that played against Arezzo last weekend. Edoardo Motta started in goal behind Romano Floriani Mussolini, Danilho Doekhi, Diogo Leite, and Alfonso Pedraza.

In midfield, Valerio Farcomeni joined Reda Belahyane in the double pivot. Club captain Mattia Zaccagni started on the left wing, with the young Federico Serra on the opposite flank, while Andrea Pinamonti led the line, with Tijjani Noslin behind him.

While the Biancocelesti held possession, they created few chances in the first 30 minutes. They eventually managed to break the deadlock at the half-hour mark when Pinamonti picked up a loose ball following a scramble inside the box and found Farcomeni on the left side. The young midfielder teed up Noslin with a perfect cross, and the Dutchman's header sailed into the far corner.

However, Lazio's lead was short-lived, as Juve Stabia levelled the score less than two minutes later from a corner kick that found no one in particular, but David Buglio was the quickest to react, slotting it past Motta from close range.

In the 39th minute, Lazio retook the lead thanks to Zaccagni. The hosts' pressing paid off, as Pedraza collected a poor pass, skipped past his marker and trotted towards the byline before feeding his captain with a back-pass. The winger's first-time attempt took a small deflection, but it was enough to upset the goalkeeper.

But once again, the Aquile failed to maintain their advantage for more than a few minutes. Fabio Maistro received the ball on the edge of the penalty box, and he found the bottom corner with a delicate shot that beat Motta.

After the break, Lazio had an inviting opportunity to lead for the third time. Juve Stabia's Substitute goalkeeper Pietro Boer played a poor pass that was intercepted by Noslin. The Lazio striker was brought down by Thomas Battistella inside the box. However, the goalkeeper was able to atone by pulling out a solid save on Pinamonti.

In the 65th minute, the visitors took the lead for the first time, as Lazio were punished by none other than their own player, Sana Fernandes. The loaned-out winger controlled a long ball expertly before prevailing in his duel against Manuel Lazzari. Finally, he chipped it past Motta before apologising to his parent club.

After wasting a penalty, Pinamonti was able to get on the scoresheet in the 78th minute. Boer committed another blunder, as he was caught napping on the ball outside his penalty box, allowing Noslin to pick his pocket. The ball reached the Italian striker, who easily directed it towards the empty net.

The Biancocelesti had several chances to find a winner, but the result remained unchanged. Gattuso will welcome back his international players next week before resuming the Serie A campaign with a home fixture against Monza on October 11.

title: 'Best midfielder in the world': Liverpool star told he's as good as Zidane
description: Liverpool have not had an overly easy time of it, results-wise, at the start of the 2026/27 season. Andoni Iraola has presided over only two victories in his opening five Premier League games - agains...
fullText:
Liverpool have not had an overly easy time of it, results-wise, at the start of the 2026/27 season.

Andoni Iraola has presided over only two victories in his opening five Premier League games - against newly promoted Ipswich Town as well as former club Bournemouth.

It is going to take a while for the Basque tactico's ideas to come across but there's no doubt we've seen promising signs already.

Alexander Isak for example is back among the goals on a more regular basis while improvements have been made to the backline too.

Liverpool are possessed of world-class talent in the midfield meanwhile - and it's only a matter of time before the Anfield side start firing on all cylinders.

The club offered new contracts to both Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai over the past few months.

Szoboszlai, 25, has hit the ground running for club AND country this season - hitting an unbelievable goal in the EFL Cup victory over Tottenham.

The Hungarian captain has carried on that fine form during the international window - excelling in the weekend win against Giorgi Mamardashvili's Georgia where Milos Kerkez scored the only goal of the game.

Szoboszlai's performance was so good in the heart of midfield that Georgian coach Giorgi Tsetsadze - in charge of top-flight side Rustavi - told Hungarian media that the Liverpool man reminded him of a certain Zinedine Zidane on the night.

"Looking at Dominik Szoboszlai, I thought of Zinédine Zidane – and not because of his hair…" he tells Nemzeti Sport.

"Seriously, his performance was almost perfect both in attack and defense.

"He was constantly looking for opportunities to pass forward, he was rushing towards the goal, trying to score, and what is especially important, he not only played forward in the middle of the field, but also gave dangerous passes in the final third.

"I think he is one of the best midfielders in the world at the moment."

Zidane is one of a select band of players to win the UEFA Champions League, the FIFA World Cup as well as the Ballon d'Or and goes down as one of the all-time greats of the game.

Iraola will be hoping to tap into those Zizou-like traits on a more regular basis once Szoboszlai returns from international duty.

description: Thousands of hours of frame-aligned, 10-player first-person gameplay with full game state — free for research, so anyone can train multiplayer world models.
fullText:
World models keep popping up. Nobody has cracked multiplayer at scale, because multiplayer data is painful to gather. It takes three things, all on the same clock:

We put in the work. Vortech is a tiny team of 3 people, racks of GPU instances, and a couple years of plumbing. Below is what came out of it.

Thousands of hours of 10-player first-person gameplay, free, so anyone can start building multiplayer world models. Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0, for non-commercial research and education.

One bot round from the dataset, recorded from all ten players at once. Every view, every number and every hit sits on the same 16 Hz clock — pick a player and watch the others see them.

The data comes from a pipeline that turns Source-engine games into unlimited multiplayer data, for anyone who holds the licence to the game, or is Valve itself. These games ship with bots and GOTV, a built-in recorder that captures every tick of every match. That is a perfect setup for automated data production: no players to recruit, no screens to capture.

First run: CS:GO, one map, 33 servers, five days. Gameplay generation scales linearly with compute. Other Source titles plug into the same steps, given the rights to them.

We have been training a multiplayer world model on this for a while.It draws the next frame for each of the ten players, while a server keeps them all in the same game.It is a work in progress; we will put it out when it is good enough.

Meanwhile, a sneak peek: the recorded game on the left, the model on the right.

Parquet + MP4, no pre-made splits, CC BY-NC 4.0 for non-commercial research. It lands on Hugging Face; this link becomes the dataset itself the day it goes up.

dataset spec get it on hugging face

Control and scale. We pick the map, the rules and the player count, and servers run around the clock. Expert bots move and fight plausibly enough to teach a model the physics, the map and the combat.

Source games record complete demos by design, replay them deterministically, and can re-render any player's view after the fact. That is what makes ten aligned POVs per match possible. And if it has to be a Source game, it might as well be CS.

Per 16 Hz step: actions, poses, health, weapons and damage events for all ten players, plus 256×256 first-person video for the rendered subset. All of it is one map, aim_map_usp_s by im0rtus, with USPs on the CT side and Glocks on the T side. That is far from enough to build a world model of Counter-Strike; it is enough to experiment with, and to focus on the multiplayer part of world models. See the dataset spec.

title: 'Different' Morrison gives NI new option
description: Northern Ireland's Kieran Morrison hopes he has earned the trust of manager Michael O'Neill after impressing on his first international start.
fullText:
Northern Ireland's Kieran Morrison hopes he has earned the trust of manager Michael O'Neill after impressing on his first international start.

The Liverpool winger, who is spending this season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, provided the assist for Isaac Price for the side's second goal in an eye-catching 3-0 Nations League win over Ukraine in Slovakia.

The 19-year-old was one of three changes made by O'Neill for the game in Trnava and impressed in an inside forward role off the right-hand side.

An unused substitute for the first two games of Group B2 in which Northern Ireland took four points against Georgia and Hungary, Morrison was pleased to quickly repay O'Neill's faith.

"I've been biding my time after the first two games," he told BBC Sport NI's Gavin Andrews.

"I was training well, working hard and I'm glad he [O'Neill] trusts me enough to give me the start. I think I did well enough."

Who has 'no ceiling' as Northern Ireland shine in Nations League?

Brown scores two as superb Northern Ireland stun Ukraine

While Price, who nodded home Morrison's cross for his 11th international goal, is nailed on for one of the roles behind the central striker in O'Neill's preferred system, Morrison certainly staked a claim to hold on to the other against Georgia at Windsor Park on Monday night.

"Thought he was really good," said Price of Morrison.

"He's a different threat than what we have had before. A really good crosser of the ball and he has come in and given the manager a headache with a game on Monday."

Despite the praise for his delivery, Morrison added that putting the ball into the box was not his first instinct.

"To be fair I wasn't going to cross it," he said.

"I was like 'OK, get the ball and do some stepovers', but it was just set it back to me and I whipped it in and Isaac was there.

"Every time I got the ball, I was just trying to make something happen."

Morrison, who represented England at underage level but qualifies for Northern Ireland through his Newry-born mother, is hoping to keep his place for Monday and make what would be a first home outing for the side.

"It's going to be great," said the player who made two senior Liverpool appearances last season.

"I've never played at Windsor Park. Hopefully I get the start, if I don't get the start, hopefully I come on and impact it."

title: Dodgers continue quest for World Series three-peat
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers will begin their MLB play-off campaign on Saturday, with the defending champions playing in a double-header live on the BBC.
fullText:
Los Angeles has been the centre of the baseball world over the past few years.

The LA Dodgers have built a star-studded roster in Major League Baseball, winning back-to-back championships in 2024 and 2025.

Celebrities and royalty have flocked to Dodger Stadium, which will also host the Olympic tournament as baseball returns to the Games for Los Angeles 2028.

And you can get a glimpse of the Hollywood vibe as the Dodgers continue their quest for a World Series three-peat in the MLB play-offs this weekend.

After earning a bye for the first round last week, it is time for the Dodgers to join the post-season party and they will be part of an MLB double-header live on the BBC.

Saturday's coverage begins with the Chicago White Sox visiting the Cleveland Guardians for the start of their American League Division Series (18:00 BST).

You can then experience all the sights and sounds from Dodger Stadium, one of MLB's most iconic venues, as the defending champions begin their National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves (21:00 BST).

Opened in 1962, Dodger Stadium is the biggest MLB arena with a capacity of 56,000, and this year 'Dodger baseball' has been one of the hottest tickets in town.

For the past two years the team's total home attendance has passed four million. This year they set a franchise record of 4,034,219 - an average of 49,805 fans per game.

The signings of two-way star Shohei Ohtani and pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto in 2024 helped boost the team's Asian fanbase, increasing Japanese tourism to LA and supplementing the loyal local support.

Actors Brad Pitt, Will Ferrell, Bryan Cranston, Jason Bateman and Rob Lowe are all regulars at Dodger Stadium, while Justin and Hailey Bieber have been spotted at multiple games.

NBA star LeBron James and NFL quarterback Justin Herbert both attended last year's World Series, along with Sydney Sweeney, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. Who will show up this weekend as LA hosts games one and two of the best-of-five series against Atlanta?

Having briefly been based in LA, Pierre Ducrey - sports director for the International Olympic Committee (IOC) - has also watched numerous games at Dodger Stadium and is "quite familiar with the atmosphere it can deliver".

"There's so many Dodger fans and they're very passionate about the team," he told BBC Sport. "They have an incredible venue and one thing I do know about baseball is this is the perfect home for a baseball tournament."

Ohtani rewrites history to send Dodgers to World Series

Why 'face of baseball' is on cusp of global stardom

The Dodgers aren't the only show in town. The LA Lakers are one of the biggest franchises in basketball's NBA, as are the LA Rams in American football's NFL.

The Rams won the Super Bowl in their own stadium in 2022 and are favourites to win the NFL's championship game when it returns to SoFi Stadium next February.

The stadium hosted eight World Cup games last summer and anticipation is growing that LA is set for a third straight World Series later this month.

"This is a city that lives and breathes sport and the Dodgers are a perfect example of that," said Ducrey. "The popularity of the franchise in LA cannot be underestimated."

Live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app

The Dodgers secured the second seed in the National League after finishing the regular season with 100 wins and 62 losses.

The Milwaukee Brewers were the only MLB team with a better record (103-59) yet the Dodgers are favourites to win the World Series, ahead of the Brewers and New York Yankees.

The Dodgers have continued to make big-name signings, with pitcher Tarik Skubal the latest in a mid-season trade, and their recent success has got fans dreaming of the franchise's first-ever three-peat.

"The Dodgers are in a very good period," Ducrey added. "There is a big momentum for them, but the team would still be immensely followed whether they're successful or not.

"There's a very long history behind it, and a very big tradition for baseball in Los Angeles."

Although Ohtani is a rare two-way player, the Dodgers' leading home-run hitter will not pitch again this year because of injuries.

Skubal is expected to start on Saturday and face Matt Olson, who led Atlanta with 41 home runs in the regular season and added another in Thursday's series-clinching win over the Philadelphia Phillies.

Either the Dodgers or the Braves will face Milwaukee or the San Diego Padres in the National League Championship Series (NLCS) - one step from the World Series.

Sixth seed Chicago have already upset the Houston Astros in the other half of the play-offs and either the White Sox or Cleveland will face the Tampa Bay Rays or Yankees in the American League Championship Series (ALCS).

The winners of the ALCS and NLCS will meet in the World Series, which is scheduled to begin on Friday, 23 October.

title: Solberg piles pressure on Evans in WRC title race
description: Elfyn Evans' hopes of claiming a first World Rally Championship title are in the balance after another strong morning for rival Oliver Solberg in Sardinia.
fullText:
Elfyn Evans' hopes of claiming a first World Rally Championship (WRC) crown are hanging by a thread after rival Oliver Solberg took the lead in the title-deciding Rally Italia Sardegna.

Solberg was again the fastest driver across Saturday morning's three stages, leapfrogging the overnight top two, Hyundai pair Thierry Neuville and Adrien Fourmaux.

The 25-year-old Swede leads Neuville by 2.7 seconds, while Evans lies in sixth place, one minute and 57.7 seconds behind the new rally leader.

The Welshman had taken a 17-point lead into the final round of the season, but on current positions that gap would be reduced to four.

With up to 10 points available as Sunday bonuses, and given Solberg's flying form in Sardinia, that puts him as the favourite to claim a maiden world title rather than his Toyota team-mate.

"A bit out of my control, I feel, with the road cleaning so much," said Welshman Evans when asked about the title race after stage 10.

"[We're] not realistically going to catch anybody in front, got to stay clean for now."

The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory

Evans on track for WRC title despite tough day

Eight-time world champion Sebastien Ogier lies third, Fourmaux fourth and Sami Pajari, who could also still win the WRC title, in fifth position.

The Finn is 42.2 seconds ahead of Evans and co-driver Scott Martin, who were again unable to match the fastest times on Saturday despite no longer facing the challenge of being the first car out on loose gravel surfaces.

Trailing 51.7 seconds behind Evans in seventh place is Josh McErlean, who lost time on stage 10 with a half-spin to avoid a tree.

McErlean's M-Sport Ford team-mate and fellow Irishman Jon Armstrong is ninth.

Evans will guarantee himself a first WRC title if he collects 19 points from the maximum 35 available to any one driver over a rally weekend.

He has averaged 19.2 points per event this season.

The winner of the rally will collect 25 points, with 17 for second, 15 for third and so on down to one for 10th place.

A further five, four, three, two and one points are available for the five quickest drivers over Sunday's four stages, with the same bonuses awarded for the fastest times on the final Power Stage.

That means any of these five scenarios would guarantee Evans his first world title.

Second overall plus at least two Sunday bonus points

Third overall plus at least four bonus points

Fourth overall plus at least seven bonus points

Fifth overall plus at least nine bonus points

If, on the other hand, Evans fails to collect 19 points this weekend, that does not mean his dream is over, but it does open the door for his rivals.

Pajari must outscore championship leader Evans by at least 18 points - in addition to gaining four more than Solberg - to take the title.

If the Finnish driver - who has won three of the past four rallies - were to take the maximum 35 points, that would mean Evans could score no more than 18.

Those returns would see the Toyota pair tied on 248 points and make Pajari champion by virtue of four rally victories this season compared to the Welshman's two.

Solberg, winner of the previous rally in Chile, needs to score at least 22 points more than Evans and five more than Pajari to take the title.

If he were to enjoy a maximum 35-point weekend and Evans picked up 15, the pair would be level on 244 points, making the Swede world champion on countback with three rally victories.

The rally continues with a further 13 stages before the winner - and the 2026 World Rally champion - is crowned on Sunday.

title: Why Bahrain is Paying Millions to Rent Malaysia’s Sepang Circuit for the 2026 F1 Season
description: If you glance at the timing screens for this weekend’s Formula 1 action, you might do a double-take. The paddock has set up camp at the iconic Sepang International Circuit in Selangor, Malaysia, yet the official event title is the…
fullText:
If you glance at the timing screens for this weekend's Formula 1 action, you might do a double-take. The paddock has set up camp at the iconic Sepang International Circuit in Selangor, Malaysia, yet the official event title is the "Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026″.

It is one of the most unprecedented logistical and financial pivots in modern motorsport history. Instead of simply canceling the race and taking a massive financial hit, the Kingdom of Bahrain opted to effectively rent an entire country's racetrack, packing up its Grand Prix and moving it 6,000 kilometers east.

Here is exactly why Bahrain is paying top dollar to host its own home race in the Malaysian jungle.

The Bahrain Grand Prix was originally scheduled to be the fourth round of the 2026 World Championship, slated for the weekend of April 10–12 at the Bahrain International Circuit in Sakhir.

However, on February 28, 2026, the outbreak of the Iran war drastically altered the global sporting landscape. Following targeted airstrikes by the United States and Israel, Iran launched counterattacks against numerous American military bases across the Middle East, including facilities located in Bahrain. By March 14, Formula 1 and the FIA officially called off both the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix due to severe safety concerns.

Losing two highly lucrative Middle Eastern markets was a massive blow to F1's revenue streams. But while Saudi Arabia's race was permanently scrapped from the 2026 calendar, Bahrain's promoters refused to let their event die.

Bahrain currently holds an ironclad contract to remain on the Formula 1 calendar until 2036. Rather than breach that contract or lose out on the massive global exposure of an F1 weekend, Bahrain's Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, orchestrated a radical alternative to show the country's "commitment to, and passion for (F1)".

Under a landmark agreement between F1, the FIA, and the Malaysian government, the race was relocated to Sepang in early October, slotting perfectly between the Azerbaijan and Singapore Grands Prix.

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 03: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands and Oracle Red Bull Racing and Isack Hadjar of France and Oracle Red Bull Racing on the fan stage prior to final practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 03, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610030108 // Usage for editorial use only //

Crucially, this is not a Malaysian Grand Prix funded by Kuala Lumpur. Bahrain is entirely footing the bill for the relocation and the massive operational costs of staging the race at Sepang. In exchange for fully financing the event, the Bahraini organizers retain complete ownership of the Grand Prix's identity, as well as 100% of the ticket pricing rights and race proceeds.

For Malaysia, it's a win-win. Sepang gets to host its first Formula 1 race since 2017 without paying F1's exorbitant multi-million-dollar hosting fees. They are simply acting as a venue supplier for Bahrain's production.

Because Bahrain owns the financial rights to the weekend, they have gone all out to ensure the event still feels like a Middle Eastern spectacle despite the tropical setting.

The organization from Bahrain flew its own staff from the Bahrain International Circuit directly to Malaysia to run the event. They are actively providing the catering, the facilities, and the VIP entertainment.

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Friday KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 02: Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 leads George Russell of Great Britain driving the (63) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on track during practice ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 02, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Sam Bloxham/LAT Images)

Fans walking around the Sepang paddock are completely immersed in Bahraini culture. The fan zone has been transformed into a "Bahrain Village," featuring authentic Middle Eastern music, crafts, and cuisine. Even the familiar paddock setups and traditional Bahraini podium ceremonies have been imported directly to Southeast Asia.

It is an incredibly bizarre sight for long-time F1 fans, but the unusual "Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia" name is entirely accurate. Bahrain didn't just sponsor a race—they literally bought a weekend on Malaysian soil to keep their Formula 1 dreams alive.

title: Joker persona helps Cong 'feel the fear' in opponents
description: Wang Cong dismisses critics who say she she is not deserving of facing Natalia Silva for the flyweight world title at UFC 332 on Saturday.
fullText:
Before Wang Cong faces off with her opponents, she dyes her hair green, paints her face white and draws a bright red grin from cheek to cheek.

Fans may assume Cong is paying tribute to Batman's notorious arch-enemy the Joker, but the Chinese fighter says her persona is rooted in the joker playing card that inspired the comic-book villain.

The 34-year-old, who is on a four-fight win streak, says she can "feel the fear" in her opponents when she wears the face paint.

On Saturday at UFC 332 in Salt Lake City, Cong will be hoping she can invoke the same emotions in Brazilian Natalia Silva, when the pair fight for the vacant flyweight world title.

"It means the most powerful card, so I want to be the most powerful," Cong tells BBC Sport.

"When I have paint on I feel crazy. It makes me perform better, it inspires me. There's not much different between paint and no paint, this is my true personality."

Cong has bewildered opponents at weigh-ins while wearing the face paint, and says she even adopts the Joker alias when using social media messaging back home in China.

She tossed an imaginary coin and pretended to shoot a gun before her fight against Gabriella Fernandes in 2024, while in July she bizarrely gifted Tracy Cortez a pack of fake eyelashes before the pair's flyweight encounter.

Cong laughs as she reveals Silva can expect a "surprise" of her own before their fight at the Delta Centre, although she then turns serious as she pays tribute to her opponent.

Silva, 29, enters the contest on a 14-fight win streak across different promotions and is the favourite to capture the vacant title after Valentina Shevchenko was forced to vacate the belt last month through injury.

"She's an incredible fighter, an eight-fight win streak in UFC, beaten three former champions, she has amazing footwork, distance control and kicks," adds Cong.

Silva, who is number one in the UFC's flyweight rankings, was set to face Shevchenko for the belt before the bout was cancelled, so was expected to challenge for the vacant title.

Some fans were surprised that sixth-ranked Cong was chosen for the title fight however, and she admits she felt the same way.

"To be honest I was a little bit surprised but if you see the rankings, the girls ranked higher than me have either a fight booked or they have just fought," said Cong.

"I'm on a four-win streak so that makes sense."

The fight represents the first women's main event in the UFC since Mackenzie Dern beat Amanda Ribas is January 2025.

The last time two women headlined one of the UFC's flagship numbered events was when Amanda Nunes defeated in June 2023.

Cong says it's "meaningful" to be flying the flag for women's MMA after a period of under representation in the UFC, and is excited for the opportunities her success could create in China.

If Cong wins, she will become only the second Chinese UFC champion after former strawweight title holder Zhang Weili.

"MMA is my final transition in my combat sports career. I think my success will encourage more athletes to be brave and try mixed martial arts in China," said Cong.

The event has received criticism from some fans on social media, who instead called for the main event to feature fighters such as Jiri Prochazka, Ciryl Gane and Alex Pereira.

When asked if Cong has a message for her critics, she was concise in her response.

"I've got nothing to say right now. After my fight I think they will shut up," she said.

title: Lewandowski and De Bruyne shine in Nations League while Džeko plays his last international game
description: Veteran stars took center stage in the Nations League on Friday with Robert Lewandowski and Kevin de Bruyne leading Poland and Belgium to victories thanks to multi-goal performances.Italy also kept Zinedine Zidane from winning in his home debut as France coach, while Edin Džeko made his last international appearance.
fullText:
Veteran stars took center stage in the Nations League on Friday with Robert Lewandowski and Kevin de Bruyne leading Poland and Belgium to victories thanks to multi-goal performances.

Italy also kept Zinedine Zidane from winning in his home debut as France coach, while Edin Džeko made his last international appearance.

De Bruyne showed he can still dominate a match at age 35 when he scored Belgium's first two goals in a 3-0 win over Turkey in League A.

De Bruyne opened the scoring 10 minutes into the game in Liege when he played a one-two with Dodi Lukébakio and struck from near the edge of the area.

The Napoli playmaker curled home another goal with half an hour to play. Substitute Romelu Lukaku sealed the win over the Turks. Lukébakio hit the post twice.

"I try to lead by example for the younger players, and they follow easily," De Bruyne said. "I feel I can still contribute. I am enjoying myself, and that is the main thing."

Belgium made it two wins and a loss — which came to France — under new coach Mark van Bommel.

When Zidane's name was read out by the stadium announcer after the teams were announced, a roar filled Stade de France.

Things looked good for the home side when Michael Olise put France ahead in the 55th minute with a curling shot from 20 meters which went in off the crossbar.

But poor defending midway through the second half allowed Italy central defender Alessandro Bastoni to run through and clip a low shot inside the right post to secure a 1-1 draw.

France leads Group 1 with seven points, followed by Belgium with six, Italy with four and Turkey with zero.

Lewandowski scored a hat trick to lead a 6-0 demolition of 10-man Romania in League B.

The 38-year-old Chicago Fire striker earned and converted a 24-minute penalty when Romania defender Radu Dragusin was sent off for fouling him in the box.

Lewandowski made it 2-0 in the 47th from a pass by Nicola Zalewski and then rounded off the lopsided victory late with his third goal.

Edin Džeko finished his nearly 20-year-international career for Bosnia-Herzegovina in a 1-1 draw with Sweden also in League B.

Džeko, 40, debuted for his nation in June 2007. He finished with 152 appearances and 73 goals, making him the record holder in both categories for the tiny Balkan nation after helping it reach two World Cups.

Džeko was given an honor guard when he was subbed off in the 63rd, shortly after Viktor Gyökeres scored for Sweden. Kerim Alajbegović equalized in the 80th for the hosts.

Also in League B, Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 3-0 in Slovakia with Ciaron Brown scoring twice.

title: NY governor says Cornell rape accuser was 'failed' by people obligated to protect her
description:
